# Evaluator reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_reference.py from the evaluator contracts (`describe_templates()`). Do not edit; run `python scripts/generate_reference.py` after changing a contract. -->

Every evaluator a criterion `type` can name, with the parameters `compile_definition` accepts. List the evaluator's template in the definition's `templates`. The same data is served by `GET /api/v1/templates`; the [definition reference](definition.md) describes the rest of a definition.

## Capabilities {#capabilities}

An evaluator runs only on a host that provides its capabilities. Both shipped hosts (the HTTP API and the GitHub Action) compose `execution_host.docker.DockerHost`.

| Capability | Shipped hosts | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox_execution` | provided | Runs the submission through a host-supplied execution session. Unavailable without execution support for the selected language. |
| `http_network` | not provided (`SERVER_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE`) | Requires a host-supplied assessed-server session covering startup, readiness, HTTP reachability and teardown. The default Docker profile fails before acquisition because it supplies no server lifecycle. |
| `ai_provider` | provided | Delegates assessment to a host-supplied AI provider. Missing provider support fails the execution before scoring. |
| `structural_analysis` | provided | Uses in-process ast-grep structural analysis of the submission source. Requires ast-grep-py to be installed and a supported language; missing analysis fails the assessment instead of scoring zero. |

## Html Css Js Template (`webdev`) {#webdev}

Static checks of HTML, CSS and JavaScript files for web development assignments.

| Evaluator | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`has_class`](#has_class) | Checks for the presence of specific CSS classes, with wildcard support, a minimum number of times. |
| [`check_bootstrap_linked`](#check_bootstrap_linked) | Checks if the Bootstrap framework (CSS or JS) is linked in the HTML file. |
| [`check_internal_links`](#check_internal_links) | Checks for the existence of internal anchor links pointing to valid element IDs. |
| [`has_tag`](#has_tag) | Checks if a specific HTML tag appears a minimum number of times. |
| [`has_forbidden_tag`](#has_forbidden_tag) | Checks for the presence of a forbidden HTML tag. |
| [`has_attribute`](#has_attribute) | Checks if a specific HTML attribute is present a minimum number of times. |
| [`check_no_unclosed_tags`](#check_no_unclosed_tags) | Detects HTML tags that were opened but not closed. |
| [`check_no_inline_styles`](#check_no_inline_styles) | Ensures that no inline styles are used in the HTML file. |
| [`uses_semantic_tags`](#uses_semantic_tags) | Checks if the HTML uses at least one common semantic tag. |
| [`check_css_linked`](#check_css_linked) | Checks if an external CSS stylesheet is linked in the HTML. |
| [`css_uses_property`](#css_uses_property) | Checks if a specific CSS property and value pair exists. |
| [`count_over_usage`](#count_over_usage) | Penalizes the use of a specific text string if it exceeds a maximum allowed count. |
| [`js_uses_feature`](#js_uses_feature) | Performs a simple string search to check if a specific feature is present. |
| [`uses_forbidden_method`](#uses_forbidden_method) | Checks and penalizes the use of a forbidden method or keyword. |
| [`count_global_vars`](#count_global_vars) | Counts the number of variables declared in the global scope. |
| [`check_headings_sequential`](#check_headings_sequential) | Checks if heading levels (h1-h6) are sequential and do not skip levels. |
| [`check_all_images_have_alt`](#check_all_images_have_alt) | Checks if all `<img>` tags have a non-empty `alt` attribute. |
| [`check_html_direct_children`](#check_html_direct_children) | Ensures that the only direct children of the `<html>` tag are `<head>` and `<body>`. |
| [`check_tag_not_inside`](#check_tag_not_inside) | Checks if a specific tag is not nested anywhere inside another specific tag. |
| [`check_internal_links_to_article`](#check_internal_links_to_article) | Checks for internal anchor links pointing to IDs on `<article>` tags. |
| [`has_style`](#has_style) | Checks if a specific CSS style rule appears a minimum number of times. |
| [`check_head_details`](#check_head_details) | Checks if a specific detail tag exists in the &lt;head> section. |
| [`check_attribute_and_value`](#check_attribute_and_value) | Checks if a specific HTML tag contains a specific attribute with a certain value. |
| [`check_dir_exists`](#check_dir_exists) | Checks if a specific directory exists in the submission. |
| [`check_project_structure`](#check_project_structure) | Checks if the expected structure path exists in the submission files. |
| [`check_id_selector_over_usage`](#check_id_selector_over_usage) | Counts valid ID selectors in the CSS. |
| [`uses_relative_units`](#uses_relative_units) | Checks if the CSS file uses relative units like em, rem, %, vh, vw. |
| [`check_media_queries`](#check_media_queries) | Checks if there are media queries in the CSS file. |
| [`check_flexbox_usage`](#check_flexbox_usage) | Checks if Flexbox properties are used in the CSS file. |
| [`check_bootstrap_usage`](#check_bootstrap_usage) | Checks if Bootstrap is being used in the HTML file. |
| [`link_points_to_page_with_query_param`](#link_points_to_page_with_query_param) | Checks for anchor tags leading to a specific page with a required query string parameter. |
| [`js_uses_query_string_parsing`](#js_uses_query_string_parsing) | Checks if the JavaScript code contains patterns for reading query strings from the URL. |
| [`js_has_json_array_with_id`](#js_has_json_array_with_id) | Checks for the existence of a JS object array where each object has a specific required key. |
| [`js_uses_dom_manipulation`](#js_uses_dom_manipulation) | Checks if the JS code uses a minimum number of common DOM manipulation methods. |
| [`has_no_js_framework`](#has_no_js_framework) | Checks for the presence of forbidden JavaScript frameworks (React, Vue, Angular). |
| [`count_unused_css_classes`](#count_unused_css_classes) | Counts the number of unused CSS classes in the HTML and/or CSS code. |

### `has_class` {#has_class}

Checks for the presence of specific CSS classes, with wildcard support, a minimum number of times.

- **Template:** `webdev`
- **Capabilities:** none
- **Languages:** any allowed language

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `class_names` | list of string | yes | — | ≥ 1 items; each item length ≥ 1 | A list of class names to search for. Wildcards (*) are supported (e.g., 'col-*'). |
| `required_count` | integer | no | `1` | ≥ 1 | The minimum total number of times the classes must appear. |

Example criterion (placeholder values; defaults written out):

```json
{
  "id": "has-class",
  "type": "has_class",
  "name": "Has class",
  "parameters": {
    "class_names": [
      "example"
    ],
    "required_count": 1
  },
  "weight": 100
}
```

## API Testing (`api`) {#api}

A template for evaluating assignments where students create a web API.

!!! warning "Not available on the shipped hosts"
    Requires `http_network`, which the HTTP API and the GitHub Action do not provide: a definition using it fails with `SERVER_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` before any sandbox is acquired.

| Evaluator | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`health_check`](#health_check) | Checks if a specific endpoint is running and returns status code 200. |
| [`check_response_json`](#check_response_json) | Checks if an endpoint's JSON response has a specific key and value. |

### `health_check` {#health_check}

Checks if a specific endpoint is running and returns status code 200.

- **Template:** `api`
- **Capabilities:** `http_network`
- **Languages:** any allowed language

!!! warning "Not available on the shipped hosts"
    Requires `http_network`, which the HTTP API and the GitHub Action do not provide: a definition using it fails with `SERVER_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` before any sandbox is acquired.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `endpoint` | string | yes | — | length ≥ 1 | The endpoint to be tested (e.g., '/health'). |

Example criterion (placeholder values; defaults written out):

```json
{
  "id": "health-check",
  "type": "health_check",
  "name": "Health check",
  "parameters": {
    "endpoint": "example"
  },
  "weight": 100
}
```

### `check_response_json` {#check_response_json}

Checks if an endpoint's JSON response has a specific key and value.

- **Template:** `api`
- **Capabilities:** `http_network`
- **Languages:** any allowed language

!!! warning "Not available on the shipped hosts"
    Requires `http_network`, which the HTTP API and the GitHub Action do not provide: a definition using it fails with `SERVER_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` before any sandbox is acquired.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `endpoint` | string | yes | — | length ≥ 1 | The API endpoint to be tested (e.g., '/api/data'). |
| `expected_key` | string | yes | — | length ≥ 1 | The JSON key to check. |
| `expected_value` | any JSON value | no | `null` | — | The expected value for the specified key. |

Example criterion (placeholder values; defaults written out):

```json
{
  "id": "check-response-json",
  "type": "check_response_json",
  "name": "Check response json",
  "parameters": {
    "endpoint": "example",
```

## Input/Output (`input_output`) {#input_output}

A template for evaluating assignments based on command-line input and output.

| Evaluator | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`expect_output`](#expect_output) | Executes the student program, providing a series of line-separated inputs and verifying if the final output is correct. |
| [`dont_fail`](#dont_fail) | Executes the student program with specific input and verifies it doesn't fail (no crash, no timeout). |
| [`expect_file_artifact`](#expect_file_artifact) | Executes the student program, then extracts a generated file from the sandbox and validates its content against expected values. |

### `expect_output` {#expect_output}

Executes the student program, providing a series of line-separated inputs and verifying if the final output is correct.

- **Template:** `input_output`
- **Capabilities:** `sandbox_execution`
- **Languages:** any allowed language

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `inputs` | list of string | no | `[]` | — | List of strings to be sent to the program, each on a new line. |
| `expected_output` | string | yes | — | — | The single string the program must print to standard output. |
| `program_command` | string or map of `python` or `java` or `node` or `cpp` or `c` to string | yes | — | length ≥ 1; each value length ≥ 1 | Command that runs the program: a nonempty string, a map with a command for every allowed language, or 'CMD' for the conventional per-language default. It runs without a shell for every test: compile in preparation.setup_commands, never here; standalone shell operators (&&, \|, ;, >, ...) are rejected. |
| `normalization` | boolean | no | `true` | — | Strip trailing whitespace from each line and normalize line endings |

Example criterion (placeholder values; defaults written out):

```json
{
  "id": "expect-output",
  "type": "expect_output",
  "name": "Expect output",
  "parameters": {
    "inputs": [],
    "expected_output": "example",
    "program_command": "example",
    "normalization": true
  },
  "weight": 100
}
```

### `dont_fail` {#dont_fail}

Executes the student program with specific input and verifies it doesn't fail (no crash, no timeout).

- **Template:** `input_output`
- **Capabilities:** `sandbox_execution`
- **Languages:** any allowed language

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `user_input` | string | no | `""` | — | Single line sent to the program's standard input; empty sends nothing. |
| `program_command` | string or map of `python` or `java` or `node` or `cpp` or `c` to string | yes | — | length ≥ 1; each value length ≥ 1 | Command that runs the program: a nonempty string, a map with a command for every allowed language, or 'CMD' for the conventional per-language default. It runs without a shell for every test: compile in preparation.setup_commands, never here; standalone shell operators (&&, \|, ;, >, ...) are rejected. |

Example criterion (placeholder values; defaults written out):

```json
{
  "id": "dont-fail",
  "type": "dont_fail",
  "name": "Dont fail",
  "parameters": {
    "user_input": "",
    "program_command": "example"
  },
  "weight": 100
}
```

### `expect_file_artifact` {#expect_file_artifact}

Executes the student program, then extracts a generated file from the sandbox and validates its content against expected values.

- **Template:** `input_output`
- **Capabilities:** `sandbox_execution`
- **Languages:** any allowed language

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `inputs` | list of string | no | `[]` | — | List of strings to be sent to the program via stdin. |
| `program_command` | string or map of `python` or `java` or `node` or `cpp` or `c` to string | yes | — | length ≥ 1; each value length ≥ 1 | Command that runs the program: a nonempty string, a map with a command for every allowed language, or 'CMD' for the conventional per-language default. It runs without a shell for every test: compile in preparation.setup_commands, never here; standalone shell operators (&&, \|, ;, >, ...) are rejected. |
| `artifact_path` | string | yes | — | length ≥ 1 | Relative path (under /app) of the file the program must generate (e.g. 'output.txt'). |
| `expected_content` | string | yes | — | — | The expected file content or pattern to match against. |
| `match_mode` | `"exact"` or `"contains"` or `"regex"` | no | `"exact"` | — | Comparison mode: 'exact' (default), 'contains', or 'regex'. |
| `normalization` | boolean | no | `true` | — | Whether to normalize line endings and trim trailing whitespace (default: true). |

Example criterion (placeholder values; defaults written out):

```json
{
  "id": "expect-file-artifact",
  "type": "expect_file_artifact",
  "name": "Expect file artifact",
  "parameters": {
    "inputs": [],
    "program_command": "example",
    "artifact_path": "example",
    "expected_content": "example",
    "match_mode": "exact",
    "normalization": true
  },
  "weight": 100
}
```

## Static Analysis (`static_analysis`) {#static_analysis}

A template for evaluating assignments through static and structural code analysis.

| Evaluator | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`forbidden_import`](#forbidden_import) | Statically analyzes submission files to check if any forbidden libraries were imported. Penalizes the submission if any forbidden imports are found. |
| [`forbidden_keyword`](#forbidden_keyword) | Statically analyzes submission files using structural analysis to detect forbidden language constructs (like loops or eval calls). |
| [`ai_sorting_algorithm`](#ai_sorting_algorithm) | Uses AI to verify that the submission implements the requested sorting algorithm rather than a library shortcut. |
| [`ai_search_algorithm`](#ai_search_algorithm) | Uses AI to verify that the submission implements the requested search algorithm rather than a library shortcut. |
| [`ai_graph_algorithm`](#ai_graph_algorithm) | Uses AI to verify that the submission implements the requested graph algorithm rather than a library shortcut. |

### `forbidden_import` {#forbidden_import}

Statically analyzes submission files to check if any forbidden libraries were imported. Penalizes the submission if any forbidden imports are found.

- **Template:** `static_analysis`
- **Capabilities:** none
- **Languages:** `python`, `java`, `node`, `cpp`, `c`
- **Passes when absent:** Prohibition: passes while none of the forbidden libraries is imported.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `forbidden_imports` | list of string | yes | — | ≥ 1 items; each item length ≥ 1 | List of library/module names whose import is forbidden (at least one). |

Example criterion (placeholder values; defaults written out):

```json
{
  "id": "forbidden-import",
  "type": "forbidden_import",
  "name": "Forbidden import",
  "parameters": {
    "forbidden_imports": [
      "example"
    ]
  },
  "weight": 100
}
```

### `forbidden_keyword` {#forbidden_keyword}

Statically analyzes submission files using structural analysis to detect forbidden language constructs (like loops or eval calls).

- **Template:** `static_analysis`
- **Capabilities:** `structural_analysis`
- **Languages:** `python`, `java`, `node`, `cpp`, `c`
- **Passes when absent:** Prohibition: passes while none of the forbidden constructs is used.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `forbidden_keywords` | list of string | no | `[]` | — | List of predefined constructs to forbid (e.g., 'for_loop', 'while_loop', 'eval_call'). At least one keyword or custom rule is required. |
| `custom_ast_grep_rules` | list of object | no | `[]` | — | List of custom ast-grep rules to apply. |

Example criterion (placeholder values; defaults written out):

```json
{
  "id": "forbidden-keyword",
  "type": "forbidden_keyword",
  "name": "Forbidden keyword",
  "parameters": {
    "forbidden_keywords": [
      "for_loop"
    ],
    "custom_ast_grep_rules": []
  },
  "weight": 100
}
```

### `ai_sorting_algorithm` {#ai_sorting_algorithm}

Uses AI to verify that the submission implements the requested sorting algorithm rather than a library shortcut.

- **Capabilities:** `ai_provider`

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `algorithm_name` | string | yes | — | length ≥ 1 | Name of the algorithm the submission must implement. |

```json
  "type": "ai_sorting_algorithm",
  "name": "Ai sorting algorithm",
  "parameters": {
    "algorithm_name": "example"
  },
  "weight": 100
}
```
